title: Reduce payment latency under burst traffic
description:
During the INC-17 incident on May 10, Payment Service experienced request timeouts due to excessive database read latency under concurrent burst load. Approximately 12% of payment transactions failed during the 11:00–11:45 UTC peak window.

Investigation shows that repeated reads of idempotency keys and payment configuration data from PostgreSQL account for 70% of query volume during bursts. These values change infrequently and are strong candidates for caching.

Proposed approach:
- Introduce an in-memory or Redis-backed cache for hot-read paths
- Measure cache-hit ratio and p99 latency improvement
- Validate that cache invalidation does not introduce stale-payment risks

Acceptance criteria:
- p99 payment latency < 200ms during simulated burst traffic
- Cache-hit ratio > 80% for idempotency key lookups
- No increase in payment inconsistency errors
